title: White Bean Chicken Chili
seoTitle: White Bean Chicken Chili | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Creamy cannellini chili with green chiles and shredded rotisserie-style chicken
subtitle: Creamy cannellini chili with green chiles and shredded rotisserie-style chicken
description: Shredded chicken simmers with cannellini beans, green chiles, cumin, and a touch of cream cheese for body. Cup-and-bowl service for the whole crew.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for White Bean Chicken Chili in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Poach and shred chicken
steps.instruction: Simmer chicken breasts in 4 cups broth 15–18 minutes until internal temp hits 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then shred into bite-size strands with two forks.

steps.title: Sweat onion and garlic
steps.instruction: In a large pot, sauté onion in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat 5–6 minutes until translucent. Add garlic and cumin; cook 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer beans and chiles
steps.instruction: Add remaining broth, beans, green chiles, oregano, and shredded chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 15 minutes so flavors meld. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Stir in cream cheese
steps.instruction: Reduce heat to low. Whisk in cream cheese cubes until fully melted and chili looks creamy with no white streaks remaining. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion White Bean Chicken Chili onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Finish with lime and serve
steps.instruction: Stir in lime juice and cilantro. Chili should coat a ladle lightly; adjust salt before cup service at the line. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Blend one can of beans for extra body without adding more cream cheese.
Hold lime and cilantro off the pot until serving so bright flavors stay fresh.
Rotisserie chicken works in a pinch—add at the end to avoid stringy overcooked breast.
tonightSpread: Cornbread muffins baked in a muffin tin.
Shredded Monterey Jack and sliced jalapeños at the line.
leftovers: Thicken leftovers into a dip with extra cheese for game-day snack.
Freeze in quart containers; thin with broth when reheating.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Lighter than red chili but still hearty. Perfect after cold-weather calls when the crew wants something warm and sippable.
mealPrepNotes: Poach chicken breasts ahead and shred. Chili thickens as it rests—add broth when reheating. Station: Keep pot on back burner at gentle simmer, not rolling boil, so cream cheese stays smooth. Station: Offer crushed tortilla chips and cilantro at a side station to keep soup texture crisp. Station: Use 12-oz bowls as default portion—crew can come back for seconds without draining the pot.
